candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Reporting of Incident/Event/Irregular Occurrence/Variance
candidate.educational_objective: After a medication error reaches a client, assess and monitor the client and complete required clinical and safety reporting even when no immediate injury is apparent.

options.A: Assess the client, follow required clinical and organizational incident-reporting processes, document the client's assessment and care factually, and continue indicated monitoring.
options.B: Withhold reporting unless the client later develops an injury or measurable adverse effect from the error.
options.C: Complete the causal investigation independently before informing the care team or using the organization's safety-reporting process.
options.D: Continue routine observation and delay formal event reporting unless symptoms or injury emerge.

candidate.rationale: The 2026 NCSBN test plan includes identifying situations where incident/event reporting is appropriate, acknowledging and documenting practice errors and near misses, evaluating the response to an error/event, and escalating unsafe practice when indicated. A no-apparent-harm outcome does not erase the need to assess the client and follow required reporting processes. Clinical documentation should remain a factual record of the client's condition, assessment, interventions, and response; the organization's separate safety-reporting process is followed according to policy.
candidate.source_claim_supported: NCSBN explicitly includes reporting of incidents/events, acknowledging and documenting practice errors/near misses, and evaluating the client's response to an error/event under Safety and Infection Prevention and Control.
candidate.source_locator: Appendix A, printed p. 25, Safety and Infection Prevention and Control → Reporting of Incident/Event/Irregular Occurrence/Variance: identify when reporting is appropriate; acknowledge/document practice errors and near misses; evaluate response to error/event/occurrence.

candidate.stem: A medication error reaches a client, but immediate assessment shows no apparent injury. Which nursing response best supports patient safety?
